questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A bubble of air is underwater at temperature $15^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and the pressure $1.5$ bar. If the bubble rises to the surface where the temperature is $25^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and the pressure is $1.0$ bar, what will happen to the volume of the bubble ?
options: Volume will become greater by a factor of $1.6$
Volume will become greater by a factor of $1.1$
Volume will become smaller by a factor of $0.70$
Volume will become greater by a factor of $2.9$
questions.solution:
(a) $\because \frac{p_{1} V_{1}}{T_{1}}=\frac{p_{2} V_{2}}{T_{2}}$ (By ideal gas equation) or $\frac{1.5 \times \mathrm{V}_{1}}{288}=\frac{1 \times \mathrm{V}_{2}}{298}\therefore \mathrm{V}_{2}=1.55 \mathrm{ V}_{1}$
i.e, volume of bubble will bealmost $1.6$ times to initial volume of bubble.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The pressure exerted by $6.0 \mathrm{ g}$ of methane gas in $\mathrm{a} 0.03 \mathrm{ m}^{3}$ vessel at $129^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ is
(Atomic masses: $\mathrm{C}=12.01, \mathrm{H}=1.01$ and $\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
$\left[$\begin{array}{l}$\text{ w(given mass$ of methane) }=6 $\mathrm{ g}$ \\ $\text{ temperature, }$ T=129+273=402 $\mathrm{ K}$ \\ $\text{ mol mass$ of methane, } M=12.01+4 \times 1.01 \\ =16.05\end{array}$\right]$
From, ideal gas equation,

$\begin{array}{l}p V=n R T \Rightarrow P=\frac{n R T}{v}$\\
$\mathrm{p}=\frac{6}{16.05} \times \frac{8.314 \times 402}{0.03}$=$41648 \mathrm{ Pa}
\end{array}$
